attack.rationale: An evidenced AD reset authority can replace the source authenticator; account manipulation is a potential behavior, not an observed reset.
The linked account has active cloud privilege and a supported AD password flow. Any cloud sign-in still requires its applicable authentication controls.

nist.rationale: Object-specific reset authority is an access enforcement decision.
Delegation to an unapproved controller expands the administrative account's privilege boundary.
The path exposes authority to replace a privileged user's source authenticator.

attack.rationale: The verified account carries effective AD control-plane membership; misuse of that domain account is potential behavior.
The same linked identity carries an active privileged cloud role. The finding shows shared standing authority, not credential compromise or a successful sign-in.

nist.rationale: The shared identity is partial evidence relevant to separation of administrative duties; it does not establish the organization's full duties matrix.
Standing authority in both administration planes widens the consequence of account control.

attack.rationale: An unapproved local administrator controls confirmed tenant-linked synchronization infrastructure and could influence hybrid identity. No modification of the authentication process is claimed.

nist.rationale: Effective local administration establishes who can control the host.
An administrator outside the approved inventory exceeds the intended host control boundary.
This is contextual evidence relevant to protecting a hybrid administration boundary; host membership alone does not assess network interface filtering or satisfy SC-7.

attack.rationale: The prospective membership change occurs in an AD domain group. This title does not describe generic cloud group edits; its use here requires the evidenced AD AddMember step.
An effective, sensitive target-service grant is connected to the synchronized group; use of resulting cloud account access is potential behavior.

nist.rationale: Source-group membership and an effective target-service grant are linked authorization decisions.
An unapproved source editor can change who receives sensitive cloud access.

attack.rationale: The evidenced source edit is to an AD domain group before synchronization. A cloud-only exclusion would require a different predicate.
A supported, complete user/resource scenario establishes a protection gap after the source group edit; this is prospective cloud account use, not a claim MFA was bypassed in a live sign-in.

nist.rationale: The source group's edit authority changes an effective access-policy exclusion.
The scenario identifies the required authentication protection and whether another enabled policy restores it.
Unapproved source-group edits can change the effective authentication exception.

attack.rationale: The evidenced effective application-owner capability allows adding a usable workload credential; no credential is generated, retrieved, or exercised.
The exact corresponding service principal has sensitive application permissions; workload account use is potential behavior. Delegated consent alone does not support this mapping.

nist.rationale: Application ownership and effective credential-write capability govern access to the workload identity.
Sensitive application permissions amplify a source-account control path into workload authority.
The owner can add an authenticator for the identified workload, subject to actual credential restrictions.
